items: When a request hits a @RestController, the DispatcherServlet delegates execution to a HandlerAdapter, which invokes the target handler method.
The method return value (be it a domain POJO, a Collection, or a ResponseEntity) is intercepted by Spring's HttpMessageConverter infrastructure.
MappingHttpMessageConverter or MappingJackson2HttpMessageConverter serializes the Java object graph into a JSON string using Jackson's ObjectMapper.
The serialized byte stream is written directly to the HttpServletResponse output stream with the appropriate Content-Type header (e.g., application/json).

parsed_answer.content: A classic production trap occurs when developers migrate a legacy application from @Controller to @RestController without auditing existing methods. If a method inside a @RestController is intended to return a legacy HTML view name string (like "dashboard"), the client will literally receive the plain text string "dashboard" instead of the rendered page because @ResponseBody forces raw string output. If your microservice architecture requires serving both REST endpoints and server-rendered administration pages, keep them cleanly separated into distinct classes utilizing @RestController and @Controller respectively.
